english.title: Practise deception intending to cause a person to leave UK and be subject to forced marriage

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: anti social behaviour crime and policing act 2014

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) practised a form of deception, namely **(..SPECIFY THE NATURE OF DECEPTION..), with the intention of causing another person, namely **(..SPECIFY PERSON..), to leave the United Kingdom with the intention that

(A)_[he]_
(B)_[she]_

be subjected to conduct outside the United Kingdom that is an offence under section 121(1) of the Anti-social Behaviour, Crime and Policing Act 2014, or would be an offence under that subsection if the victim were in England or Wales
english.legislation: Contrary to section 121(3) and (9) of the Anti-social Behaviour, Crime and Policing Act 2014.

with the intention of causing a person to leave the UK
and be subjected to conduct outside the UK that is an offence under s.121(1) /

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) A person commits an offence only if, at the time of the deception -
(a) the person or the victim or both of them are in England or Wales,
(b) neither the person nor the victim is in England or Wales but at least one of them is habitually resident in England and Wales, or
(c) neither the person nor the victim is in the United Kingdom but at least one of them is a UK national

other.penalty:
Summary: Twelve months imprisonment and / or a fine
Indictment: Seven years imprisonment and / or a fine

Important Note:
In relation to an offence committed before paragraph 24(2) of Schedule 22 to the Sentencing Act 2020 comes into force (01/12/20), the reference to 12 months imprisonment in relation to summary offences, above, is to be read as a reference to 6 months imprisonment.

Time Limit for Prosecutions:
None
